summary: Feed s133_double to APM is degraded: 18.4% of TCP sessions are one-way and 38.4% of frames arrive inside VXLAN tunnels, both preventing complete transaction visibility.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction for 19 of 103 TCP sessions (18.4%). Most likely asymmetric routing with separate ingress TAPs/SPANs not aggregated, or a load-balancing/hash policy that sends client->server and server->client to different tool ports. APM requires both directions on the same port.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM cannot correlate request/response pairs, cannot compute latency, transaction time, or TCP handshake RTT, and will misclassify 18% of sessions as incomplete/failed, degrading application performance monitoring coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same APM tool port using bidirectional flow hashing so the APM sees complete sessions.

findings.root_cause: 568 of 1478 frames (38.4%) are VXLAN-encapsulated and forwarded still encapsulated. Packet broker is not stripping VXLAN headers before delivery to the APM, so the tool sees outer tunnel headers instead of inner application traffic.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM cannot parse inner IP/TCP and L7 headers, misses application transactions inside the overlay, and loses visibility on 38% of traffic for performance and error detection.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to terminate/strip VXLAN encapsulation and forward only the inner frames so APM can decode application transactions.
